tagline: The wealthiest stretch of the US Atlantic Intracoastal — a year-round ultra-HNW and finance-relocation market just north of Miami.
summary: The Palm Beach corridor is the natural northward extension of Navier's Miami beachhead and arguably its richest single market: Palm Beach and Manalapan hold the highest concentration of US ultra-HNW waterfront residences, and the post-2020 finance migration to West Palm Beach has thickened a year-round executive-commute base along the Intracoastal. The ICW links Boca Raton, Delray, Palm Beach, Singer Island, Jupiter and the Treasure Coast (Stuart / Sailfish Point) in a continuous sheltered waterway, while bridge openings and I-95 / US-1 congestion make a fast water tier genuinely time-competitive. It connects south to Fort Lauderdale and Miami in Pioneer II range for a continuous Gold-Coast all-electric corridor.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns the entire Atlantic ICW corridor: Palm Beach ↔ Jupiter, Boca, Stuart, and the Gold-Coast connector to Fort Lauderdale and Miami — all comfortably in all-electric range.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR is not required here; the corridor is a dense Pioneer II network. Quanta-LR is available for any future offshore Bahamas leg from the Treasure Coast.

competitive_landscape: Private center-console and superyacht charter fragment the leisure layer; there is no scheduled fast-water incumbent. Bridge-tender schedules are the main operational friction. Uber is the demand-platform partner; the West Palm finance cluster is the B2B base.
seasonality: Year-round demand, strongest in the Nov–Apr 'season' when the Palm Beach social and finance calendar peaks. Atlantic hurricane season (Jun–Nov) raises offshore sea state but the sheltered ICW stays workable.
regulatory_note: US Coast Guard Subchapter T inspection; Florida clean-marina and manatee/no-wake zones favor zero-emission, low-wake operation in the ICW; ICW drawbridge scheduling is the key operational constraint.
